title: Fantasy football Week 5 stock watch: Buy low, sell high and win your trades - CBS Sports
description: Drake Maye bounced back, Kyler Murray found his rhythm and Ashton Jeanty struggled on the ground as we sort throu
body:
Drake Maye bounced back, Kyler Murray found his rhythm and Ashton Jeanty struggled on the ground as we sort through key buy-low and sell-high trade targets across the league
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Week 5 was a wild one for Fantasy Football action. Let's take a look at some of the key takeaways, winners, losers, buy low and sell high candidates as we move forward. Jacksonville 19 – Philadelphia 17WINNER: Jalen Hurts, QB, EaglesAn encouraging game for him, even if the numbers don't show it. The 40 pass attempts really stand out. Could the Eagles start throwing more, even when Saquon Barkley returns? The schedule is about to be GREAT for Hurts. I'm not saying buy low because the Eagles offense has some warts, but this was a step in the right direction.Green Bay 31 – Chicago 7WINNER, I GUESS?: Marshawn Lloyd, RB, PackersMaybe Josh Jacobs returns soon, but as long as he remains out, Marshawn Lloyd is the best option in the Packers backfield. He averaged 3.1 yards per carry against a bad Bears run defense, so I'm not getting too excited. All of Kaleb Johnson's carries were in garbage time.FLUSH IT AND FORGET IT: The Bears offenseCaleb Williams could return next week and they will start rocking and rolling again.
New York Giants 27 – Washington 27SELL HIGH: Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, CommandersHe had a great game, which included a 33-yard TD run on the opening possession. It's certainly possible that Jayden Daniels opens this offense up for him, but the Giants are a great matchup. The schedule is about to get much tougher. He rarely catches a pass. I say "sell high (if you can)" because I'm not sure anyone is buying.WINNER: Anyone with NFL clock management experience. The Commanders are hiring.New England 45 – Las Vegas 17WINNER: Drake Maye, QB, PatriotsHe's back. I'm an idiot for doubting him.LOSER: MeI doubted Drake MayeNOT SURE HOW I FEEL ABOUT HIM: Ashton Jeanty, RB, Raiders10 carries for 27 yards, but of course, six targets and 50 receiving yards. He has not been efficient as a rusher. I bet his managers are panicking. He also came into the game nicked up. I might want to buy low. Listen to the Fantasy Football Today Podcast this week to find out!Pittsburgh 34 – Indianapolis 22LOSER: Josh Downs, WR, ColtsCan't trust him. He's a WR3. Downs will have good games in the future, but they will be hard to predict. Also, Keenan Allen had more targets. Not cool!
WINNER: Jaylen Warren, RB, SteelersThis guy is awesome. The Steelers always want to use two RBs, and Jaylen Warren is always the better guy. Rico Dowlde could be back next week, but Warren should be featured. I suppose I'd trade him for Ashton Jeanty, since I think Dowdle will have something of an annoying role, but if you have Warren on your team, I think you're going to be happy.Cincinnati 31 – Miami 24LOSER: Chase Brown, RB, BengalsWe might have a problem here. He fumbled, and Samaje Perine started getting more work. The Bengals are going into their bye and I fully expect Chase Brown to be their lead back after the bye, but the lack of rushing yards and lack of overall production is concerning. Remember, he had 11 catches last week with Ja'Marr Chase injured.WINNER: Ollie Gordon, RB, DolphinsI must say, I'm surprised and impressed. Two good-to-great games in a row for Gordon. I do think he's a clear winner and someone you can trust as a flex, but you can also try to sell high. Zero catches in these two games. Shoot for the stars
Houston 26 – Tennessee 3WINNER: CJ Stroud, QB, TexansStroud has scored at least 20.5 points (6 point per passing TD leagues) in every game with Nico Collins. He's worth using in good matchupsLOSER: Carnell Tate, WR, TitansJust when you thought you could trust him! The Texans were allowing the most points to WRs, but I'm not buying that this is a good matchup. We know who the Texans are when they are right. I expect Tate to bounce back. Don't drop himMinnesota 23 – New Orleans 13WINNER: Kyler Murray, QB, VikingsFinally, we see a game with Kyler Murray and Justin Jefferson, and it's Murray's best game of the season. Keep in mind, he didn't have Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson left almost immediately with a concussion. Murray ran for 51 yards. He could definitely be a streamer going forward.
FLUSH IT AND FORGET IT: The SaintsIt was the Vikings. Next week, they get the Giants. All will be forgotten.New York Jets 17 – Cleveland 12LOSER: The weatherCan we get a Sunday in New York/New Jersey with good weather? Some of us would like to go outside.POTENTIAL LOSER? Breece Hall, RB, Jets Braelon Allen was awesome in this game. Is he carving out a bigger role for when Breece Hall returns? I'm not convinced yet, but another good game next week at New England would make me nervous if I had Hall.

title: Bengals vs. Dolphins bad beat: Missed extra point decides spread in Cincinnati win - CBS Sports
description: Riley Patterson's missed extra point off the upright seale
body:
Riley Patterson's missed extra point off the upright sealed a 31-24 win for Cincinnati, handing -6.5 spread bettors an improbable cover
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The Cincinnati Bengals took a trip to South Beach in Week 5, hoping to snap a two-game skid against the winless Miami Dolphins. The Bengals closed as seven-point favorites at most sportsbooks, and 6.5-point favorites at others. A Bengals cover didn't feel in doubt through the majority of the game.By halftime, the Bengals had acquired a 14-point lead thanks to three passing touchdowns from star quarterback Joe Burrow. That lead increased to 18 points by the time we reached the fourth quarter after a 45-yard touchdown reception by Ja'Marr Chase.However, Malik Willis trimmed the Bengals' lead to 10 points with a touchdown pass to Kevin Coleman Jr., and a successful two-point conversion toss to Greg Dulcich with seven minutes remaining in the final quarter. Following a Bengals punt, defensive tackle Jonathan Allen stripped Willis of the ball deep in Dolphins territory and recovered it at Miami's 10-yard line. It looked like the game was well in hand.The Dolphins then held the Bengals to a 26-yard field goal, which increased Cincinnati's lead back to 13 points. Willis then took his offense 61 yards down the field and punched in a one-yard touchdown to trim the deficit to seven points with under one minute to play.
Since a two-point conversion wouldn't do anything, the Dolphins trotted out Riley Patterson for the extra point in hopes of making it a six-point game. Then, the Dolphins could try for the onside kick. But Patterson doinked the kick off the left upright! 
The Dolphins couldn't recover their onside kick, and the Bengals took two kneel-downs to secure a 31-24 victory! Bengals -6.5 bettors scored a wild win, while the +7 bettors out there at least got a push. Talk about a bad beat for those backing the Dolphins +6.5! 
The 3-2 Bengals are off to their best five-game start since 2021, the year they reached the Super Bowl, while the 0-5 Dolphins just became the fifth team since 1950 to not hold a lead in any of their first five games.

schema.headline: Bengals vs. Dolphins bad beat: Missed extra point decides spread in Cincinnati win - CBS Sports

title: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza makes NFL debut: A look at how No. 1 overall pick performed - CBS Sports
description: The Raiders rookie QB was solid out of the gate in the Raiders' blowout loss
body:
The Raiders rookie QB was solid out of the gate in the Raiders' blowout loss
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It took until Week 5, but the 2026 No. 1 overall pick got to make his NFL debut. Down 45-17 in the fourth quarter against the New England Patriots, the Las Vegas Raiders opted to put Fernando Mendoza in to replace Kirk Cousins, marking the rookie's first appearance in the regular season. Mendoza took over for Cousins, who went 19-of-28 for 243 yards and one touchdown, with just over six minutes remaining. The 2025 Heisman Trophy winner had a solid start, starting off 5-for-5, including a 16-yard pass on Vegas' final drive of the game.The 23-year-old threw his first incompletion on 1st-and-10 on the Patriots' 20-yard line, followed by a 6-yard pass that set up 3rd-and-4 on the New England 14-yard line. An incomplete pass set up fourth down, and with nothing to lose, the Raiders went for it.Mendoza scrambled and had a decent run, but fell just short of the line to gain, prompting a turnover on downs and an eventual victory formation for the Patriots. The No. 1 overall pick's final stat line was 6-of-8 for 48 yards, with no touchdowns, picks or sacks taken.
Mendoza began the season as Cousins' backup and became the first No. 1 overall selected quarterback to not start Week 1 since 2018 (Baker Mayfield).Heading into this week, Cousins was tied for the league high in passing touchdowns with 11.The Patriots extended their win streak to two games and improved to 3-2 with the 45-17 win. The Raiders, who were one of the league's last remaining undefeated teams, are now 3-2, dropping their last two wins. Both teams have faced difficult AFC opponents the last two weeks, with the Patriots defeating the Buffalo Bills in Week 4 and the Raiders falling to the Kansas City Chiefs last week.
The Raiders have another challenge next week, when they face the Bills.

schema.headline: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza makes NFL debut: A look at how No. 1 overall pick performed - CBS Sports

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade grades: Cardinals extract near-max value from Texans for former top-5 pick WR - CBS Sports
description: Arizona dealt Harrison Jr. for multiple draft picks, including a 2027 second-round pick
body:
Arizona dealt Harrison Jr. for multiple draft picks, including a 2027 second-round pick
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The awkward separation between wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and the Arizona Cardinals is now complete. He is now a Houston Texan after his new team reportedly sent multiple draft picks to Arizona in exchange for the fourth overall pick from the 2024 NFL Draft. Houston shipped a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Cardinals in exchange for the 24-year-old wideout and a 2027 seventh-round draft choice. Harrison Jr., the son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison, is now the first wide receiver since Ahmad Rashad in 1974 to be traded within his first three years in the NFL after being selected as a top-five pick, per CBS Sports Research. Rashad was also traded from the Cardinals and was shipped to the Buffalo Bills in exchange for quarterback Dennis Shaw.   WRs traded within first three seasons as top-five picks in Common Draft era (Since 1967)19742026Wide receiverAhmad RashadMarvin Harrison Jr.Overall pick4th4thTraded fromCardinalsCardinalsTraded toBuffalo BillsHouston TexansTrade compensation receivedQB Dennis Shaw2027 2nd-round pick, 2027 6th-round pickSo, who came out with the better haul in the exchange? Here are trade grades for both the Texans and the Cardinals in terms of how they made out in the deal. Houston Texans: C-The Houston Texans are grasping at straws in 2026. They are 1-4 and enter the late afternoon games in Week 5, averaging the second-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) and the fewest rushing yards per carry (3.0) by a team's running back group in the entire league. Houston's disappointing start has nothing to do with quarterback C.J. Stroud. His 280.4 passing yards per game rank as the fourth-most in the NFL entering the Week 5 late afternoon games, and his 6-0 touchdown-to-interception ratio is tied for the second-best in the league. Stroud's 185 throws without an interception are now the fourth most in the league through four games in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. That's why the Texans have made their second wide receiver trade of 2026 after dealing safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the New England Patriots this offseason in exchange for veteran wide receiver Kayshon Boutte. Stroud will be asked to put the Texans' offense on his back this season, so why not trade for a former collegiate target of his? He and Harrison Jr. were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history.  Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston also needed another wide receiver to make an impact outside of two-time Pro Bowler Nico Collins, since once-exciting wide receiver Tank Dell's NFL career was sidetracked by a significant knee injury.  Dell went down in Week 16 of the 2024 season with a dislocated kneecap, torn ACL, LCL, MCL, and meniscus damage, and he hasn't played a game since. Most receiving TD in a season, Ohio State historyReceiving TDTerry Glenn (1995)17Jeremiah Smith (2024)15Marvin Harrison Jr. (2023)14Marvin Harrison Jr. (2022)*14*David Boston (1997)14* C.J. Stroud was Ohio State's starting QB in 2022Houston was desperate and filled a need, but what it spent to acquire Harrison is a little rich, given the writing was on the wall that Harrison Jr.'s Cardinals' career was coming to an end. Arizona Cardinals: B+The Cardinals did about as good a job as they could to recoup value for Harrison Jr., with everyone and their grandma aware that Harrison Jr.'s time in Arizona was a bust and about to end. A second-round pick in the vaunted 2027 NFL Draft is ideal. Plus, they moved up a round at the back of the draft, sending a 2027 seventh-round pick along with Harrison Jr. and getting a 2027 sixth-round pick back.Despite racking up 202 targets in Arizona, the third-most on the team since 2024, he totaled just 108 catches for 1,578 yards receiving and 13 receiving touchdowns while failing to build a consistent rapport with both Kyler Murray and Jacoby Brissett. He trailed only McBridge (362) and Wilson (241) in targets on the Cardinals since entering the league.Arizona could have earned an A- or an A if it had gotten a first-round pick in return for the former top-five pick. Harrison Jr. is under team contract for up to a maximum of three more seasons on his rookie deal, including the rest of 2026. That's a decent value for a team that believes all he needed was a change of scenery. However, what the Cardinals did receive back was solid, all things considered.

title: Commanders vs. Giants ends in tie after Washington's overtime clock-management blunder - CBS Sports
description: A furious Dan Quinn watched the Commanders waste their chance to win after Jayden Daniels went down with eight se
body:
A furious Dan Quinn watched the Commanders waste their chance to win after Jayden Daniels went down with eight seconds left in overtime
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Washington Commanders and the New York Giants played to the NFL's first tie of the season, a 27-27 finish. The Commanders stunningly ran out of time in a complete meltdown at the end of the extra session. Here's the final play:
The Commanders -- who had no timeouts -- were extremely casual, letting the clock run after the previous play. They had absolutely no reason to run the clock down, considering it was a next-score-wins situation. The blunder created a surreal scene: Giants defenders jumping for joy as if they had won, Commanders players slouched over in disbelief and Dan Quinn absolutely furious.
He has no one to blame but himself. The play appeared to be a Jayden Daniels pass, but the quarterback never threw the ball and then went down. With eight seconds left when Daniels went down, Washington could not line up for a spike in time, a shocking failure for a team that was fortunate to be in the situation anyway. Again, Washington had no reason to even run any play other than a spike. In fact, they didn't even need that. They could have simply had Drew Stevens attempt the game-winning kick from roughly 41 yardsHow the Commanders ended up in this positionThe Giants trailed 27-13 with less than eight minutes left in regulation before two Jameis Winston touchdown passes forced overtime. New York got the ball to start overtime and drove into Washington territory before Dominic Zvada missed a 46-yard field goal.
The Giants forced a quick three-and-out, though, and went on another long drive, this time in a next-score-wins scenario. The Giants were at the Washington 24-yard line -- well inside Zvada's range -- but wanted to get closer, given that kicker Zvada had missed three field goals at that point. But Daron Payne punched the ball out from Cam Skattebo, an inexcusable mistake from the Giants' running back.
Skattebo couldn't have known it then, but it only turned out to be the second-worst mistake of the afternoon. The Commanders not knowing the situation is truly atrocious on every level -- from Quinn to offensive coordinator David Blough to Daniels -- and an absolute gut punch for a team that had hoped Daniels' return from a dislocated elbow would provide a spark. Instead, it resulted in one of the most shocking errors anyone will see at the professional level and more scrutiny on Quinn and the entire organization.The Giants (3-1-1) still lead the NFC East and, in fact, even gained a half-game on the field with the Cowboys and the Eagles both losing. The Commanders go to 1-3-1 in embarrassing fashion.
What Dan Quinn, Jayden Daniels said after gameBoth Quinn and Daniels addressed the media after the game and took responsibility for the blunder."We all gotta do better situationally, football starts with me, everybody will say the same thing but we just gotta be better at situational football," Daniels said. "We gotta stop the clock, we gotta know that it's 'o zone' situation, we gotta relay that as an offense. It starts with everybody, top down, ultimately it's on me."But Quinn took all the blame."After the first down run, still trying to gain more for the kick. Right call is honestly we can go clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot, and that's my responsibility, nobody else's."
But if the initial goal was to get closer, Quinn made two mistakes. Washington ran its penultimate play -- a two-yard Rachaad White carry -- with 55 seconds left in overtime, more than enough time to run multiple more plays, even without a timeout. And again, this cannot be stressed this enough: Washington had no reason to run the clock down. The Giants weren't going to get another possession if Stevens made his kick. And if it's yards Washington wanted, there was no reason to take so long between White's run and the final play, which started with 12 seconds left; even running any non-spike play at that point is risky.Once the clock had run down so far, the final play was supposed to be a spike or a throwaway, Quinn said. Instead, it was neither."The sequencing of that does not fall on [Daniels]," Quinn said. "It's an out-of-bounds throw or a clock. That has to come from me. I don't even need to put him into that spot."

title: Seattle vs. San Francisco: 49ers' Dre Greenlaw ejected after head-butting Seahawks' Ernest Jones - CBS Sports
description: A late hit on Sam Darnold along the Seattle sideline spark
body:
A late hit on Sam Darnold along the Seattle sideline sparked a confrontation that ended with the San Francisco linebacker head-butting a helmetless player
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Seattle Seahawks vs. San Francisco 49ers has been one of the best rivalries the NFL has had to offer in recent years, but things went a bit too far during the second quarter of their Week 5 matchup.49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw drew a flag for a late hit on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold along the Seattle sideline. He was then confronted by several Seahawks players, including linebacker Ernest Jones. During the confrontation, Greenlaw head-butted the helmetless Jones, which led to his ejection. Check out what happened here:
Greenlaw is one of the 49ers' best players on defense, and entered this matchup ranked second on the team in tackles with 34. He's also their emotional leader. That was on full display during San Francisco's Week 4 victory against the Denver Broncos last Sunday, when he confronted his former head coach Sean Payton, telling him to "Get the f--k off the field." He was also fined $11,941 by the league for taunting the Broncos' bench. "He was fired up all week," George Kittle said of Greenlaw last Sunday. "I think you could've asked anybody who played with Dre Greenlaw for his first four or five years he was here, I think 90% of the roster would say that he was their favorite teammate."
As evidenced by Sunday, sometimes that emotion can have unwanted ramifications. Greenlaw received a one-game suspension last season when he ran after an official and jawed at them following a game-winning field goal. Officials have also ejected him twice in previous games. Greenlaw was kicked out of a game in 2022 following a helmet-to-helmet hit on Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, and then during the 2022 playoffs, when he famously got into an altercation with Philadelphia Eagles head of security Dom DiSandro.

title: Will the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade unlock his potential? History offers hope, and a warning - CBS Sports
description: The Arizona Cardinals felt they were getting their next star receiver when they drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. at No. 4 overall in the 2024
body:
The Arizona Cardinals felt they were getting their next star receiver when they drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. at No. 4 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft and now, less than three years later, the team is moving on. The Cardinals finalized a deal to trade the former Ohio State star to the Houston Texans.Harrison was told on Saturday that he would be inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions as the details of the trade were finalized. The Harrison experiment certainly didn't go the way either side expected, as 1,000-yard seasons seemed ahead of him and frequent trips to the end zone felt like a guarantee. When Harrison joined the league after such a successful run with the Buckeyes, it didn't take much imagination to envision what the two-time unanimous All-American's NFL career might look like and the future looked hopeful. Thirty-three games later, we're having a very different conversation: Will Harrison be better off playing somewhere other than Arizona?
Maybe. And soon we will find out. Trading for Harrison requires believing two things for the Texans: that the Cardinals haven't gotten the most out of him, and that another team can do better. The first argument is getting easier to make. The second is where things get complicated, especially when you look at what's happened to other highly drafted receivers who fell short of expectations early in their careers.The No. 4 pick comes with expectationsIn my recent story on Carnell Tate, the fourth pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, we looked at what teams should expect from receivers drafted in the top 10. The average rookie season over the last decade was 901 receiving yards. Harrison finished with 885 in 2024, a respectable start, even if it fell short of expectations.But things haven't gotten better. Harrison managed 608 yards in 12 games last season, and through four games in 2026, he has five catches for 85 yards. For perspective, Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price, who played three games before landing on IR, has four receptions. This is the same Price who was targeted just 14 times over his final two seasons at Notre Dame. Harrison was targeted at least 13 times in four different games during his final season at Ohio State.
So yeah.Through 33 NFL games, Harrison has 1,578 receiving yards. Amari Cooper, also drafted fourth overall, had 2,285 yards at the same point. Corey Davis, the fifth pick in 2017, had 1,503. Harrison's production looks much closer to Davis's than Cooper's.Harrison vs. first-round receivers early in their careersStatisticHarrison1st-round WR avg.Rank (53 WRs)Receiving yards/game47.853.033rdReceptions/game3.273.7335thReceiving TD/game0.390.3017thCatch rate53.5%59.3%46thYards/target7.818.2231stYards after catch/reception2.54.5T-51stExplosive catches/target20.8%18.4%9thThere are encouraging numbers here. Harrison's 13 touchdowns are more than Cooper (12) or CeeDee Lamb (11) had through their first 33 games. He's also ninth in explosive receptions per target. But he's near the bottom in catch rate and yards after the catch. The big plays are there; the consistent production isn't.Harrison was playing more, but producing lessPerhaps the biggest concern isn't simply that Harrison has struggled. It's that he became less involved in Arizona's offense, even while playing more.Among 41 first-round receivers in their first four appearances of Year 3, Harrison ranks 39th in receiving yards and is tied for the fewest receptions.Harrison's disappearing opportunitiesStatisticFirst 29 games2026 (4 games)Typical Year 3 1st-round WRReceiving yards/game51.521.364.8Targets/game6.53.37.5Catch rate54.5%38.5%60.9%Routes/game31.835.532.3Targets per route20.5%9.2%22.7%That last row tells the story. Harrison was targeted on roughly one of every five routes through his first 29 games. This season, it's fewer than one in 10. And that raises a fair question: Is Harrison struggling because he isn't getting opportunities, or is he not getting opportunities because he's struggling?There's evidence for both. Harrison ran 17 go routes in the first two games, tied for sixth most in the league, and Jacoby Brissett took some responsibility after Harrison went without a catch. But we can't blame everything on the quarterback or scheme when Trey McBride and Michael Wilson have combined for 58 receptions through four games. Harrison has five.Getting better isn't the same as becoming a starDespite the social-media noise, I'd be careful about giving up on Harrison. Plenty of first-round receivers have needed time to develop, but there's a difference between becoming productive and becoming the player a team thought it was drafting.Corey Davis, Mike Williams and DeVante Parker all improved after modest beginnings. Each had at least one season that justified some of that early optimism. The problem? None consistently produced like the elite receiver his draft position suggested. And Davis was drafted the highest of the three, at No. 5 overall, one spot after Harrison.Then there's Lamb, who went from a good young player to one of the NFL's best. But he was already averaging more than 62 yards per game through 33 appearances, considerably better than Harrison's 47.8.How other first-round WRs developedWR (draft pick)First 33 games YPGGames 34+ YPGNotable later seasonMarvin Harrison Jr. (4th)47.8TBDTBDCorey Davis (5th)45.555.9984 yards (2020)DeVante Parker (14th)44.748.71,202 (2019)Mike Williams (7th)35.751.41,146 (2021)Marquise Brown (25th)48.143.61,008 (2021)CeeDee Lamb (17th)62.690.41,749 (2023)Amari Cooper (4th)69.266.01,250 (2023)Williams and Parker eventually had 1,000-yard seasons, and Davis nearly got there with 984 in 2020. Harrison is young enough to make a similar leap. But Cooper and Lamb were already much more productive at this stage. That's an important distinction.What a trade can (and can't) fixSo what happens when a first-round receiver gets a fresh start somewhere else?Amari Cooper is the obvious success story. In 2018, Oakland traded him to Dallas, where his production jumped from 46.7 to 80.6 yards per game. He followed that with consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. Brandin Cooks also flourished after New England acquired him from New Orleans in 2017, producing 1,082 yards before adding 1,204 with the Rams the following year.But here's the difference: Both Cooper and Cooks had already posted two 1,000-yard seasons before being traded. Their new teams weren't betting on production they'd never seen. They were building on what those receivers had already done.The other historical comparisons aren't nearly as encouraging.I looked at first-round receivers traded in Year 3 or Year 4, the same stage of Harrison's career. Some joined better offenses or played with better quarterbacks. Most never became the players their new teams hoped they would.First-round WR trades in Years 3-4: Price and productionReceiverTraded from → toTrade returnBefore tradeAfter tradePhillip Dorsett (2017)Colts → PatriotsJacoby Brissett528 yards (2016)194 (2017)290 (2018)397 (2019)Corey Coleman (2018)Browns → Bills7th305 (2017)Released by BUF71 with NYG (2018)Jalen Reagor (2022)Eagles → Vikings7th + conditional 4th/5th299 (2021)104 (2022)138 (2023)100 (2024)Jahan Dotson (2024)Commanders → Eagles3rd + two 7ths; 5th sent with Dotson518 (2023)216 (2024)262 (2025)Brandin Cooks (2017)Saints → Patriots1st + 3rd; 4th sent with Cooks1,173 (2016)1,082 (2017)1,204 (2018)583 (2019)Sammy Watkins (2017)Bills → RamsE.J. Gaines + 2nd; 6th sent with Watkins430 in 8 games (2016)593 (2017)519 (2018)673 (2019)Kelvin Benjamin (2017)Panthers → Bills3rd + 7th475 in 8 CAR games217 in 6 BUF games380 (2018)Amari Cooper (2018)Raiders → Cowboys1st280 in 6 OAK games725 in 9 DAL games1,189 (2019)1,114 (2020)N'Keal Harry (2022)Patriots → Bears7th184 (2021)116 (2022)no rec (2023)Hollywood Brown (2022)Ravens → Cardinals1st; 3rd sent with Brown1,008 (2021)709 (2022)574 (2023)91 in 2g (2024)Cooper is the clearest example of a receiver taking his game to another level. Cooks maintained his production, while Sammy Watkins remained useful without ever returning to his 1,000-yard form.But Dorsett, Coleman, Reagor, Dotson and Harry? None became the player their original teams envisioned. Injuries played a role in some cases, but changing teams didn't solve the larger problem. And that's something Harrison's new team should keep in mind when setting their expectations. The price needs to reflect the gambleOf course, there's another reason Harrison is appealing: his contract. His new team will inherit his remaining 2026 salary and 2027 compensation, with the possibility to exercise his fifth-year option for 2028.But what should it cost to acquire him? Houston parted with a pair of 2027 draft picks, one in the second round and another in the sixth.The historical returns vary considerably. Dallas sent a first-rounder for Cooper. New England gave up a first and third for Cooks, getting a fourth back. Arizona surrendered a first for Hollywood Brown, with a third coming back. All three receivers had already proved themselves.Meanwhile, Dotson cost a third and two sevenths, with a fifth going the other way. Harry and Coleman each brought back seventh-round picks.Harrison falls somewhere in between. He wasn't going to fetch a first-rounder, but a third felt closer to his worth given his production and untapped potential. But remember, Pittsburgh got a 2028 second-round pick for Joey Porter Jr. when plenty of people thought a third was the best-case scenario.Put another way: You never know. If Houston believes it can unlock Harrison, a second-rounder might feel like a bargain. But at that price, whoever the mystery buyer is, better have a plan for using him.The gambleI think Harrison can be better than he's been in Arizona. We all saw what he did at Ohio State, and we've seen flashes of that ability in the NFL. The issue has been consistency.The tougher questions are how much better he can be, and what another team should give up to find out.Cooper showed that a change of scenery can work. But history also shows how often a fresh start changes very little, particularly for receivers who haven't already established themselves as consistently productive.

schema.headline: Will the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade unlock his potential? History offers hope, and a warning - CBS Sports

title: Nick Sirianni accepts blame for Eagles' London loss: 'I lost us that game' - CBS Sports
description: Philly made a controversial decision with eight seconds remaining in the fourth quarter that ultimately cost them
body:
Philly made a controversial decision with eight seconds remaining in the fourth quarter that ultimately cost them a win
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles lost their third straight game on Sunday, falling to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, 19-17. Despite all the players who had retired, been traded or were out with injury this week, the Eagles found themselves in position to defeat one of the hottest teams in the AFC. However, a controversial decision with eight seconds remaining in the game led to a deflating loss.With 1:35 remaining in the fourth quarter, down two points, Jalen Hurts led the offense 32 yards down the field on nine plays, setting Jake Elliott up with a chance at a 48-yard field goal. He nailed it, putting the Eagles up, 17-16, with eight seconds left on the clock. On the ensuing kickoff, the Eagles decided to leave the ball in play instead of kicking it into the end zone, allowing Ameer Abdullah an opportunity to pick up some yards. Abdullah made the play of the game, breaking loose for 53 yards to set Cam Little up with a game-winning 57-yard field goal. 
After the game, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni accepted blame for the decision to leave the kickoff in play and for the loss as a whole. "I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that's what I said to our guys, and what hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game," Sirianni said. "I put that fully on me."
Sirianni was asked about his thought process behind his decision to kick a returnable ball, but he didn't want to elaborate. One could assume the Eagles wanted to allow a few of the eight seconds to run off the clock as the Jaguars returned the ball. However, you can't allow the returner to break loose for 53 yards.The 2-3 Eagles are now under .500 for the first time since 2021. Sunday's loss snapped a franchise-record streak of 76 games where the Eagles were .500 or better, per CBS Sports Research. The last time the Eagles were under .500, Jason Kelce was the starting center, A.J. Brown was on the Tennessee Titans, Aaron Rodgers was still with the Green Bay Packers and Tom Brady was in his second-to-last NFL season. Overall, it's been a bad couple of weeks in the city of Philadelphia.

title: What Commanders' Dan Quinn, Jayden Daniels said after end-of-game mistake in tie vs. Giants - CBS Sports
description: Daniels took accountability for the mishap, saying ultimately, it's on him
body:
Daniels took accountability for the mishap, saying ultimately, it's on him
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Washington Commanders just needed to stop the clock with enough time to kick a field goal, and they had a good chance to defeat the New York Giants in the final seconds of overtime. Instead, what happened was a comedy of errors. The Commanders ran out of time, and the divisional game ended in a 27-27 tie, the first tie of the 2026 season.On second-and-8 with 12 seconds remaining, quarterback Jayden Daniels scrambled, found no one open and held on to the ball.  He went down around the line of scrimmage with about eight seconds to go. The one thing the Commanders' offense needed not to do on that play was keep the ball in bounds and allow the clock to continue to wind.With no timeouts remaining, time ticked down as the Commanders scrambled to get the ball lined up and snapped, hoping to spike it with enough time to kick about a 41-yard field goal.They didn't have nearly enough time.
What Washington should've done was kick the field goal on second down, as the next score would win the game anyway. Instead, they got "cute," as they say, and tried to give themselves a few more yards, not just failing there, but losing any chance to win the game.
After the game, Daniels and Quinn addressed the mishap and explained, or did their best to explain, what happened.What Daniels had to sayDaniels took responsibility for the mistake and noted that everyone needs to improve."We all gotta be better situationally. Starts with me," Daniels said. "Everybody will say the same thing, but we just gotta be better at situational football."
When asked what his goal was on the play that ate up all their time, Daniels said, "We've got to stop the clock... We've gotta relay that as an offense. It starts with everybody — top down, but ultimately it's on me."He was then asked if he heard anything or said anything in the huddle about not having a timeout, but he didn't give much away on whether the offense was clued into their situation."Um, just got to be better, just got to be better," he said. What the head coach saidHead coach Dan Quinn didn't place the blame solely on Daniels, also taking accountability for putting his team in that situation. He said he hadn't spoken to Daniels about it yet, but said, "It falls on me." Quinn complimented Daniel's performance outside of the final play, adding that his QB made some incredible plays and showed why "he's so unique."
He emphasized that he didn't need to put Daniels in the space to make such a mistake, noting that they could've won it then. "At the end, I can make life easy there," Quinn said. "We didn't need to gain more yards."The head coach said he himself feels frustrated and is frustrated for the team. While it may read as a tie in the standings, Quinn said it feels like a loss.
One play doesn't win or lose a game, but when it's so jarring and handled so poorly, it can feel that way. The Commanders had other chances to set themselves up to win, so they wouldn't need to be in a position to kick a game-winning field goal.The Commanders fell to 1-3-1 and are in last place in a struggling NFC East division. The Giants fell to 3-1-1 and are in first place in the division, thanks to the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys both losing this week.Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers in Week 6.

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade: Cardinals send former top-5 pick to Texans for multiple draft choices - CBS Sports
description: Harrison Jr. reunites with his Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud in Houston after a failure to launch in Arizona
body:
Harrison Jr. reunites with his Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud in Houston after a failure to launch in Arizona
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Arizona Cardinals' divorce with 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is actually happening. Arizona is trading the 24-year-old, along with a 2027 seventh-round pick, to the Houston Texans for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick, according to ESPN. Texans head coach confirmed the trade on Sunday, following Houston's first win of the year, a 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans.The trade was announced during the Cardinals' game against the Detroit Lions, a game in which Harrison was inactive due to the pending trade. Rumors swirled over the weekend that a trade could be imminent, and now Harrison will get a fresh start after his time with the Cardinals didn't go as expected. Texans quarterback and Harrison's former Ohio State teammate C.J. Stroud was asked about the trade after his game. "You want to know more? I don't know what more I can tell you," Stroud said with a smile. "I think he's a great guy, think he's a great player, and I'm excited to get him here."
The Texans were one of the top teams in the conversations surrounding a Harrison trade, in large part due to the wide receiver's connection with Stroud. The two played at Ohio State together in 2021 and 2022. On Saturday, as the trade rumors were taking over the league, CBS Sports' Aditi Kinkhabwala spoke with Stroud about Harrison."[Stroud] told me [Harrison's] an amazing talent, he told me he's a great teammate, he said that he still believes in what he can do. And he also said he's one of the hardest workers he's ever known ... Stroud said sometimes a fresh start can be really good," Kinkhabwala said.If Stroud and Harrison can replicate, or even come close to replicating, what they did together at Ohio State, the Texans' offense will see a dramatic improvement. Harrison set or tied career-highs in receptions (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in 2022 at Ohio State with Stroud at the helm.
Harrison Jr. struggled to stand out for the 1-3 Cardinals early in 2026 with five catches for 85 yards receiving and a touchdown. His five catches are tied for sixth on Arizona, ranking behind All-Pro tight end Trey McBride (33), wide receiver Michael Wilson (25), wide receiver Kendrick Bourne (13), rookie running back Jeremiyah Love (11) and running back Tyler Allgeier (10). For his Cardinals career, he totaled 108 catches for 1,578 yards receiving and 13 receiving touchdowns despite 202 targets, the third-most on the team since 2024. He trailed only McBridge (362) and Wilson (241) in targets in the span of his young career. The Texans need another wide receiver to emerge for Stroud, aside from two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Nico Collins, with once-promising wide receiver Tank Dell's career derailed by injury. Dell went down in Week 16 of the 2024 season with a dislocated kneecap, torn ACL, LCL, MCL, and meniscus damage, and he hasn't suited up since. Harrison Jr., the son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison, is now the first wide receiver since Ahmad Rashad in 1974 to be traded within his first three NFL seasons after being selected in the top five of the NFL draft, per CBS Sports Research. Rashad was also traded from the Cardinals and was sent to the Buffalo Bills in exchange for quarterback Dennis Shaw. 
Harrison is also now the fifth top-5 pick to be traded before year four in the past 10 years. The others in the same category are quarterback Zach Wilson (traded from the New York Jets to the Denver Broncos in 2024), quarterback Trey Lance (traded from the San Francisco 49ers to the Dallas Cowboys in 2023), cornerback Jeff Okudah (traded from the Detroit Lions to the Atlanta Falcons in 2023) and quarterback Sam Darnold (traded from the Jets to the Carolina Panthers in 2021).Defending Super Bowl champion Darnold is the only player on the list to see actual success in their career after their initial trade, though it did take many stops before he got there.

title: Kentucky fined $500K by SEC after fans storm field to celebrate wild overtime win vs. Lane Kiffin's LSU squad - CBS Sports
description: The Wildcats were fined for violation of the leagues's access to competition area policy
body:
The Wildcats were fined for violation of the leagues's access to competition area policy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Kentucky's successful two-point conversion in overtime to beat LSU 35-34 on Saturday night was a costly one after thousands of students poured onto Kroger Field celebrating the program's epic victory.The SEC has fined the Wildcats $500,000 — which is owed directly to LSU — for violating the league's access to competition area policy after fans stormed the field.It's a not-so-small price to pay for Kentucky's first home victory over a top-10 team since the 2021 season and marks first-year coach Will Stein's second such win of the campaign.The Wildcats surged from unranked to No. 15 in Sunday's Week 7 AP Poll as a result.
The SEC's policy states that "institutions shall limit access to competition areas to participating student-athletes, coaches, officials, support personnel and properly credentialed or authorized individuals at all times.  For the safety of participants and spectators alike, at no time before, during or after a contest may spectators enter the competition area."
        
            
                LSU's road woes continue as Kentucky stuns No. 10 Tigers, adding pressure to CFP hopes
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Moments after Kentucky kicker Adam Zouagui forced overtime in the final minute of regulation, the Wildcats opted to go for the win on a successful two-point conversion for the second consecutive game. Quarterback Kenny Minchey ran through the middle of LSU's defensive front untouched in the Wildcats' four-wide look for the victory.Zouagui had previously missed two chip-shot field goals in the fourth quarter before forcing the extra session with 1:30 left in the contest.
"That's the life of a kicker," Stein said in his post-game press conference. "You've got everybody watching you on those kicks. It was unfortunate that he missed two, but he hit a really big one. We do pressure kicks all the time in practice. I've seen him hit it a million times. He did a great job in that moment."The league eliminated its escalating fines policy ahead of the 2025 season in favor of a more direct, costly punishment for field storming situations."The motivation was 'field rushing is field rushing, the first time or the 18th time,'" SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said last spring. "The random nature of, if you're the one getting rushed, it doesn't feel good. It might be the first time (it happened) there, but it might be your sixth time in a row, literally."
Under the previous system, SEC schools were fined $100,000 for the first offense, $250,000 for the second offense and $500,000 for any violations of the rule thereafter. The SEC also now has the authority to waive a fine if the visiting team and game officials are allowed to return safely to their respective locker rooms before fans enter the playing area. According to the league office, the SEC's access to competition area policy "allows for member institutions to adopt an institutional policy that permits fans to celebrate on the playing surface once all visiting team personnel and game officials have safely exited the field or court.  The school must submit the plan to the Conference office in advance and communicate the policy to fans. If all visiting team personnel and game officials are safely off the playing surface prior to fans entering the field or court, then the home institution may avoid the prescribed penalty."

schema.headline: Kentucky fined $500K by SEC after fans storm field to celebrate wild overtime win vs. Lane Kiffin's LSU squad - CBS Sports

        Welcome to the Week 5 grades!If we learned one thing this week, it's that the NFC East might want to send every head coach in the division to some sort of coaching clinic. There are four teams in that division, and somehow none of them won in Week 5, even though there was a game between two NFC East teams. This entire week has been an absolute nightmare for the coaches in the division. 
It started on Thursday with the Cowboys looking unprepared in their stunning 24-16 loss to the Buccaneers. On Sunday morning, the Eagles went to London and lost because Nick Sirianni didn't ask his kicker to boot it out of the end zone after Philadelphia went up 16-14 on a field goal with eight seconds left to play. On Sunday afternoon, Dan Quinn topped both of them by letting his team run out the clock when they were in range for a potential game-winning field goal in overtime. The clock hit zero before the Commanders could spike the ball to give their kicker a 42-yard game-winning field goal attempt. Instead, the game ended in a tie. With that in mind, let's get to this week's grades, starting with the tie in Washington.  Giants (3-1-1) 27-27 tie with Commanders (1-3-1)Patriots (3-2) 45-17 over Raiders (3-2)Packers (3-2) 31-7 over Bears (3-2)Steelers (3-2) 34-22 over Colts (2-3)Texans (1-4) 26-3 Titans (0-5)Bengals (3-2) 31-24 over Dolphins (0-5)Vikings 23-13 over SaintsJets (2-3) 17-12 over Browns (3-2)Jaguars (4-1) 19-17 over Eagles (2-3) in LondonBuccaneers (1-4) 24-16 over Cowboys (2-3)

        Texas dropped five spots in the Week 7 Coaches Poll to No. 6 after falling 27-24 to rival Oklahoma in the Red River Showdown on Saturday. The Longhorns came in one spot ahead of Alabama, which held steady at No. 7, despite falling 20-17 at home to Georgia.The Bulldogs claimed the No. 1 spot and received 60 of 74 first-place votes, edging No. 2 Notre Dame, No. 3 Miami and No. 4 Indiana. No. 5 Ohio State also received a first-place vote after improving to 5-1 with a 45-16 win over Maryland. LSU retained a spot in the poll at No. 21 after falling to 4-2 with an overtime loss at Kentucky. The Wildcats rose from No. 25 to No. 17 after improving to 4-1.The biggest roster this week was UCLA, which surged 10 spots to No. 12 after improving to 5-0 with a 17-15 win at Oregon. Remarkably, the Ducks dropped 12 spots but stayed in the poll at No. 25 after falling to 3-2.
